quarterly_data.quarter: LS Cable & System press release: release ls-eb-a7-88-eb-a6-b0-ec-86-94-eb-a3-a8-e (10-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: LS Marine Solution (release on LS Cable & System's newsroom) is loading at Donghae port, onto its cable-laying vessel GL2030, the submarine cable for the Langkawi project in Malaysia, its second overseas power project after Taiwan Power Company's offshore wind farm (TPC2); GL2030 will sail to Malaysia and is expected to complete laying within the year. The project, won by LS Cable & System from Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), links the mainland and Langkawi island with a 132kV submarine cable. It is GL2030's first project since its upgrade from the 4,000-ton class to the 7,000-ton class, which lets it lay more than 100km of submarine cable continuously. With the recent KRW 156.9 billion Sinan Ui submarine-cable order, the order backlog has grown to about KRW 820 billion, more than three times 2025 annual revenue of KRW 244.2 billion; with GL2030 deployed, all three of its vessels are in operation (the others on submarine-cable installation and maintenance in Taiwan and the Pacific). A company official: LS Marine Solution holds Korea's only HVDC submarine-cable installation track record and will expand its participation in core grid projects including the West Coast energy highway.
